item.title: Nikko Yumoto Onsen: A Milky Sulfur Hot Spring in the Highlands — Guide
item.description: Nikko Yumoto Onsen sits at the far end of the Okunikko highland route, beside a small volcanic lake, with a history of hot spring use said to stretch back over 1,200 years to a Buddhist priest’s discovery of the sulfur waters. The distinctive milky white, sulfurous baths are believed to soothe skin ailments and fatigue, and the compact onsen town’s remote, mountain-ringed setting offers a genuinely quiet retreat, a marked contrast to the busier lower reaches of Nikko.

item.title: Senjogahara Marshland: A High-Altitude Boardwalk Through Nikko's Wilderness — Guide
item.description: Senjogahara (‘battlefield plain’), named for a legend of a mythical battle between the deities of Mount Nantai and Mount Akagi, is a high-altitude marshland in the Okunikko highlands above Lake Chuzenji, sitting at roughly 1,400 m elevation. Wooden boardwalks wind through the wetland, protecting the fragile ecosystem while offering relatively easy hiking with views toward the surrounding mountains, wildflower meadows blooming through summer, and golden-brown grasses in autumn creating an atmospheric, open contrast to Nikko’s densely forested shrine areas.

item.title: Nikko Nature: Kegon Falls, Lake Chuzenji & Okunikko
item.description: Tochigi’s natural landscape is dominated by the mountains and waterways of Nikko National Park. Within a 30-kilometre arc north of Nikko town, the terrain rises from cedar forest through alpine lake shoreline to open highland marshland and active volcanic ridges. The concentration of natural features — waterfalls, caldera lake, wetland plateau, gorge — within a single day-trip area from Tokyo is unusual even by Japanese standards. This guide covers the main natural destinations in order of access from Nikko town, with practical details on transport, access costs, and the best times to visit each.
